items.title: Head of Arab list appointed temporary deputy speaker of Israel's parliament
items.author: MEE staff
items.preview: Head of Arab list appointed temporary deputy speaker of Israel's parliament Submitted by MEE staff on Mon, 11/16/2026 - 13:50 Ahmad Tibi, who served as deputy speaker between 2006 and 2022, secured the position despite facing opposition from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Pale
items.content: Head of Arab list appointed temporary deputy speaker of Israel's parliament Submitted by MEE staff on Mon, 11/16/2026 - 13:50 Ahmad Tibi, who served as deputy speaker between 2006 and 2022, secured the position despite facing opposition from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Palestinian lawmaker Ahmad Tibi speaks to supporters in Ara, northern Israel, on 23 October 2026 (Ahmad Gharabli/AFP) Off Palestinian lawmaker Ahmad Tibi was appointed temporary deputy speaker of Israel 's parliament on Monday, securing a prominent position after parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel made significant gains in last month's election. The Times of Israel reported that the Knesset's Arrangements Committee approved a list of nine temporary deputy speakers by 13-9 votes following a heated debate. It said the the approved deputy speakers were Tibi, who chairs the Joint List alliance and leads the Ta'al party, United Arab List (Ra'am) MP Walid Taha, B'Yachad MP Eitan Ginzburg, Democrats MP Yair Fink, Yisrael Beytenu MP Oded Forer, United Torah Judaism MP Yitzhak Pindrus, Likud MP Yaakov Bardugo, Otzma Yehudit MP Limor Son Har-Melech and Shas MP Michael Malkieli. According to the Times of Israel, the temporary deputies will serve until permanent deputy Knesset speakers are appointed. It also reported that the during the debate, Likud MP Ofir Katz accused the committee of "normalising terror supporters," while Otzma Yehudit MP Yitzhak Kroizer called the appointments a "Rubicon that must not be crossed." Speaking to Al Jazeera after the vote, Tibi said that his appointment was a "rightful achievement" for the alliance, which secured 11 seats in the 27 October election. The Joint List and Ra'am, which represent Palestinian citizens of Israel, won a combined 19 seats in the 120-member parliament, marking a significant increase in their representation. Speaking to Al Jazeera, Tibi accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party and National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir of attempting to prevent his election, saying they had failed despite what he described as "reckless incitement". "The Joint List will be represented in all committees," he said. Following the elections, allegations have swirled that Netanyahu and members of his office sought to undermine Arab political parties. On Sunday, Tibi called for a criminal investigation into Netanyahu and his aides, accusing them of engaging in "mafia-style conduct" following an investigative report by Israel's Channel 12 television. Palestinian parties must not help Eisenkot rescue Israel from collapse Read More » The report alleged that Netanyahu's chief of staff, Ido Norden, contacted the police commissioner’s office ahead of the election, claiming that three Ra’am activists in southern Israel were carrying large sums of cash and vouchers intended to influence voters. Police subsequently raided the activists' homes and arrested them, reportedly relying on information from an intelligence source who was a former employee of the prime minister’s office. The report also alleged that Shin Bet chief David Zini sought permission to wiretap the phones of five Arab lawmakers on election day. Israel's attorney general reportedly rejected the request. "No one is above the law, not even Netanyahu," Tibi wrote on X on Sunday, calling for an investigation into the allegations. The prime minister's Likud party has denied the accusations. Tibi, who was first elected to the Knesset in 1999, previously served as deputy speaker between 2006 and 2022. Several Palestinian and Arab lawmakers have held the position, including Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas, who served from 2020 to 2022. The Joint List has backed former army chief Gadi Eisenkot in his efforts to form Israel’s next government after President Isaac Herzog tasked him with the job earlier this month. Neither Eisenkot’s alliance nor Netanyahu’s bloc secured the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority, leaving the support of Arab-led parties potentially decisive in the negotiations. items.title: 'I may not return alive': In open letter to top judges, Imran pleads for medical treatment for him and Bushra Bibi
items.author: none@none.com (News Desk, Ikram Junaidi)
items.preview: ISLAMABAD: Incarcerated PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan on Monday appealed for medical treatment for himself and his wife Bushra Bibi in an open letter to the chief justices of the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), the Supreme Court (SC) and the Islamabad High
items.content: ISLAMABAD: Incarcerated PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan on Monday appealed for medical treatment for himself and his wife Bushra Bibi in an open letter to the chief justices of the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), the Supreme Court (SC) and the Islamabad High Court (IHC). The letter was shared on the social media platform X by Imran’s lawyer Barrister Salman Safdar, who had met the ex-premier at Adiala jail on Nov 2 and Nov 11 . The letter said that during the Nov 11 meeting, Imran had directed Safdar to “carry his words to your lordships”. “I have conveyed this letter faithfully and solely on these instructions. The words that follow are his [Imran’s],” the letter said, which also bore Safdar’s signature. In the letter, Imran detailed his own deteriorating health condition as well as his wife’s, pleading with the courts to grant them access to medical treatment. “I spent my life building hospitals so that those who could not afford treatment would receive it free of cost. Today, I ask only that my wife and I be treated,” he said. Imran said that he was writing from a “solitary cell”, as that was now “the only way my voice can leave these walls”. “I do not write as a former prime minister, nor as the head of a political party. I have given my life to Pakistan. I served this nation on the cricket field, in social work and philanthropy and as its 22nd prime minister. For seventy years, not a single criminal case stood against my name,” he said. “Then, after the age of 70, came an unprecedented and ruthless campaign of political victimisation: countless prosecutions, more than a hundred appearances before the courts, pre-arrest bail sought again and again, and an assassination attempt which, by the grace of Allah, I survived. Through all of it, I chose the path of law. I decided that I would fight every one of these politically motivated cases in the courts and I never stopped,” he said. He said that from “time to time” he was granted relief from the courts that “renewed my faith that justice would prevail”. “After the constitutional amendments, however, that relief became narrow, and then it closed off altogether. It grieves me deeply to say that, when I needed it most, the system I had placed my trust in did not come to my aid. Within the walls of Adiala, my wife and I have faced criminal trials one after the other, and our appeals still await decision. Yet I have never once sought relief on medical grounds, nor used illness as a tactic. I fought on the merits, with confidence, and I still do,” he said. Imran went on to say that “everything changed” after the judgement in the Toshakhana-2 case. The ex-premier and his wife were sentenced to 17 years in jail in the case, which pertained to the purchase of an expensive Bulgari jewellery set, gifted to Imran by the Saudi crown prince during an official visit in May 2021, at a throwaway price. “I was totally isolated, disconnected and held incommunicado from the outside world, in torturous solitary confinement for up to twenty-two hours a day, in disregard of every constitutional right and every entitlement the Prison Rules guarantee a prisoner: no family, no lawyers, no call to my sons, no books and no television,” Imran said in his letter. He said that after months without access to his lawyer, Safdar was allowed to meet him on Feb 10 after the SC appointed him amicus curiae. “He found that I had lost 85 per cent of the vision in my right eye and that neither my family nor my counsel had been told. After that visit, the disconnect returned, and the jail administration, acting vindictively, isolated me once again,” he said. Imran said that he had only been allowed to meet his lawyer four times during the year, while Bushra Bibi had only been allowed to meet her counsel once. He asserted that this was a violation of the rules and the basic rights of every prisoner, adding that it had left them “unable to defend ourselves in the very cases we are fighting”. “Prolonged solitary confinement and the absence of any meaningful human interaction have taken a heavy toll on my mental health. This is not my claim alone: the jail’s own medical board has recorded my anxiety and advised more frequent contact with my wife and family, reading material and television. That advice has not been followed,” he said. Imran alleged that his weekly meeting with his wife was skipped by jail authorities “without reason or explanation”. He said that he had also learnt that his sisters were in custody, adding that he was not allowed to meet them. He said his sons, Kasim and Sulaiman, were also not allowed to call in contradiction of court orders. “No one in the jail is permitted to respond to me or speak to me, not when I offer them salaam and not when I recite a verse of the Holy Quran. The purpose, I can only conclude, is to make me ill and to break my will,” he said. Imran said that despite this, he was more concerned about Bushra Bibi’s conditions. He said that in April, she suffered a retinal detachment and underwent a “complicated eye surgery in secrecy” and was sent back to solitary confinement. “When I saw her this month, she could neither bear the light nor open her eyes, and without another surgery she may lose her sight permanently. Her records are withheld, her doctors denied, her suspension of sentence unheard, despite the law’s compassion for women prisoners,” he said. Imran said that on Aug 18, the SC directed that he be shifted to Shifa International Hospital within two days , a medical board be constituted to examine him and that he be allowed interactions with his family. “That order has not been implemented. My case now rests on the docket of the FCC, awaiting a hearing,” he said. He said that his appeal in the Al-Qadir trust case was being taken up ahead of older ones concerning the health of the couple and unimplemented court orders. “It is my wife’s failing sight, and that unimplemented order of the honourable SC, that compel me to write. In solitary confinement, my blood pressure has become uncontrolled: 130, then 150, then 170, and last week 192 and 193 on Nov 10. The doctors now tell me that I am highly vulnerable to a brain haemorrhage and cardiac arrest and that my heart has already suffered damage. At 74, this unrelenting state is taking me to a place from which I may not return alive,” he said. “I have fought impossible legal battles in countless cases, and I have not stopped. But the system has stopped giving me justice,” he lamented. “I do not ask your Lordships for any favour. All I request as justice is the implementation of the orders of the honourable SC and proper treatment for our medical conditions. I will only remain able to prove my innocence if I stay alive. I appeal to your Lordships, on the most basic grounds of human compassion: give me justice before it is too late,” he concluded. ‘Incredibly harrowing’ Meanwhile, Imran’s son Kasim said in a post on X that it was “devastating to read this letter from my father”. His other son, Sulaiman, described the letter as “incredibly harrowing”. “My father’s appeal to receive proper medical care is in no way a request for special treatment. It is the absolute bare minimum required to comply with internationally recognised standards for human rights,” he said. He called on authorities to shift Imran to Shifa International hospital for treatment “before it is too late”. The leaders of the opposition in the National Assembly and the Senate, Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas expressed “grave concern, sorrow and regret” over the conditions and treatment described in Imran’s letter, calling it a “test for our entire justice system”. “It is deeply regrettable that a former prime minister who has consistently approached the courts to face the cases against him and fight his legal battles is now compelled to appeal to the higher judiciary through an open letter merely to secure his basic human needs, medical care and the right to meet his family,” they said in a joint statement. “The fundamental responsibility of the state and the relevant authorities is to ensure the protection of every person in custody’s life, health and human dignity, not to add to their difficulties and suffering,” they said. The joint statement also termed the concerns regarding Bushra Bibi “profoundly regrettable”. “We strongly urge the higher judiciary to take immediate notice of all the matters raised in Imran’s letter and take effective judicial action to protect his life, health, liberty and fundamental rights,” the opposition leaders said. They clarified that their demand was “not for any special concession or extraordinary facility, but for compliance with the Constitution, the law and court orders”. Speaking to Dawn , PTI Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram called on the courts to take notice of Imran’s letter. “His case should also be seen on humanitarian grounds and medical treatment for him and Bushra Bibi should commence immediately,” he said. We urge the court to take notice and provide legal rights to Imran without further delay,” he said. ‘Claims contrary to facts’ Meanwhile, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said that claims regarding the “denial of medical facilities, treatment and other basic amenities in prison are contrary to the facts”. “Imran being provided with the necessary facilities, including meals of his choice, books and television. In fact, he is currently among the most privileged prisoners in Pakistan,” the minister said. “His health is reviewed and monitored weekly by qualified medical specialists. Whenever required, he is also examined at leading medical facilities outside the prison,” he said. Chaudhry added that Imran had been taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences “eight times for medical examinations, where doctors declared his health satisfactory”. “A doctor from London, who also practises in Pakistan, was specifically called to examine his blood pressure. According to the medical assessments, his blood pressure is satisfactory,” he said. “It is the government’s responsibility to ensure proper healthcare, medical supervision and protection of the legal rights of Imran, just as it is for every other prisoner. The government has neither neglected his medical care in the past nor will it allow any negligence in the future,” he said. The minister said that the PTI should refrain from turning a “sensitive matter like Imran’s health into a political propaganda campaign and should instead present facts responsibly”. “Political narratives cannot overturn legal proceedings or provide anyone with an escape from legal accountability,” he said. Imran and Bushra Bibi’s health Imran has been in prison since August 5, 2023 , while his wife was arrested on January 17, 2025, in a separate case in which the couple were sentenced. The IHC has allowed Imran twice-a-week meetings — on Tuesdays and Thursdays — with his family, lawyers and other associates. Despite multiple court directives , Imran’s meetings with his family and party leaders have been largely restricted . Imran’s eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion — came to light in late January, following which he has been taken to hospital multiple times. On Aug 18, the SS directed the government to shift the jailed ex-premier to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad, a day after the superintendent of the Adiala jail — where Imran is imprisoned — submitted a report to the court on the ex-premier’s health condition. However, the government took the PTI founder to Pims and subsequently transported him back to prison. At the time, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar had blamed “the security situation created by PTI workers on the way to and outside” the hospital for the diversion. The PTI has denied the allegations and accused the government of deliberately flouting the court’s orders. Meanwhile, Bushra Bibi suffered a retinal detachment in April and was taken to the hospital for surgery . She has since approached the courts seeking an immediate medical examination by an ophthalmologist and permission to receive treatment from doctors of her choice at her own expense amid concerns over her deteriorating eyesight. According to the former first lady, doctors who examined her had diagnosed her condition as a “mature cataract” and advised that another eye surgery would be required.

items.author: NOS Nieuws
items.preview: De belangstelling bij Nederlanders in het buitenland om mee te beslissen over de samenstelling van Eerste Kamer is de afgelopen vier jaar fors gegroeid. Het aantal Nederlanders expats dat zich heeft aangemeld, bedraagt nu al meer dan 82.000. Aan de vooravond van de Staten- en Eer
items.content: De belangstelling bij Nederlanders in het buitenland om mee te beslissen over de samenstelling van Eerste Kamer is de afgelopen vier jaar fors gegroeid. Het aantal Nederlanders expats dat zich heeft aangemeld, bedraagt nu al meer dan 82.000. Aan de vooravond van de Staten- en Eerste Kamerverkiezingen in 2023 waren dat er zo'n 37.500. De verkiezingen voor de Eerste Kamer zijn indirect. Nederlanders die in Nederland wonen, kiezen bij de Statenverkiezingen leden van hun provinciale parlement: de Provinciale Staten. De gekozen Statenleden kiezen twee maanden later de leden van de Eerste Kamer, normaal gesproken zijn dat kandidaten van hun eigen partij. Nederlanders in het buitenland of de overzeese gemeenten Bonaire, Sint-Eustatius en Saba vallen niet onder een provincie. Daarom zijn voor hen speciale kiescolleges in het leven geroepen. Voor Nederlanders in het buitenland is dat het kiescollege niet-ingezetenen, inwoners van de overzeese gemeenten hebben hun eigen kiescolleges . Wie zich bij een kiescollege registreert , kan per brief een stem op een kandidaat voor dit kiescollege uitbrengen. De leden van die kiescolleges brengen vervolgens hun stem uit voor de Eerste Kamer, net als Statenleden in de provincies dat doen. Het kiescollege niet-ingezetenen doet dat in Den Haag. De eerstvolgende Statenverkiezingen zijn op 17 maart volgend jaar. De Statenleden kiezen op 24 mei de nieuwe Eerste Kamer. Registreren voor het kiescollege niet-ingezetenen kan nog tot 3 februari volgend jaar. Op 15 november van dit jaar woonden de meeste geregistreerde expats in Duitsland (14.701), gevolgd door België (13.076) en Frankrijk (7.328). In 2023 konden Nederlanders in het buitenland voor het eerst meebeslissen over de samenstelling van de Eerste Kamer. GroenLinks was toen de grootste partij onder Nederlanders in het buitenland, met bijna 18,5 procent van de stemmen. D66 kreeg 16,3 procent en VVD 14,3 procent.

items.content: حذّرت هيئات معنية بتنظيم السلامة النووية تمثل 38 دولة، اليوم الإثنين، من تزايد خطر وقوع حادث نووي في أوكرانيا خلال فصل الشتاء، داعيةً روسيا إلى وقف هجماتها على البنية التحتية للطاقة في البلاد، والتي تعتمد عليها المحطات النووية لتشغيل أنظمتها بأمان. وتكثّف موسكو هجماتها بالطائرات المسيّرة والصواريخ على منشآت الطاقة الأوكرانية، بما فيها المحطات وخطوط الكهرباء ومحطات التوزيع الفرعية، في وقت تعرّضت فيه شبكة الطاقة لأضرار متكررة منذ اندلاع الحرب قبل نحو خمس سنوات. تحذير من تزايد مخاطر السلامة النووية وقالت الهيئات، في بيان مشترك اطّلعت عليه "رويترز" قبل نشره: "نعبر معاً عن قلقنا البالغ إزاء المخاطر المتزايدة على السلامة النووية الناجمة عن الحرب التي تشنها روسيا ضد أوكرانيا، وهجماتها المستمرة على البنية التحتية للطاقة في البلاد". وأضافت أن هناك "ضرورة ملحة لأن توقف روسيا هجماتها على المنشآت النووية الأوكرانية والبنية التحتية للطاقة الضرورية لتشغيلها بأمان". ويتمثل القلق الرئيسي في أن انقطاع إمدادات الكهرباء المستقرة من الشبكة قد يعرقل قدرة المحطات النووية الأوكرانية على تبريد موادها النووية، ما يزيد خطر حدوث انصهار وتسرب مواد مشعة، على غرار ما وقع في كارثة تشرنوبل عام 1986، التي تُعد أسوأ حادثة في تاريخ الطاقة النووية المدنية. وأدى حادث تشرنوبل إلى انتشار مواد مشعة في أجزاء من أوكرانيا وبيلاروسيا وروسيا وشمال أوروبا ووسطها. خطر بلوغ ذروته هذا الشتاء وقال بير ستراند، رئيس رابطتين من الهيئات المشاركة في إصدار البيان، في مقابلة مع "رويترز"، إن الهجمات الروسية أصبحت أكثر فتكاً خلال الأسابيع الماضية، مشيراً إلى استخدام موسكو طائرات مسيّرة تحمل حمولات أكبر وتتمتع بدقة أعلى في الاستهداف. وأضاف: "بسبب هذه الأساليب الجديدة التي يتبعها الروس، من الواضح أن خطر وقوع حادث نووي سيبلغ ذروته هذا الشتاء". وأوضح أن أسوأ السيناريوات يتمثل في انهيار شبكة الكهرباء الأوكرانية على مستوى البلاد، بما يؤثر في الوقت نفسه على المفاعلات النووية التسعة العاملة في أوكرانيا. وقال: "تعطّل تسعة مفاعلات في الوقت نفسه مع احتمال حدوث تسرب إشعاعي سيشكّل وضعاً خطيراً للغاية". وشدّد ستراند على ضرورة اتخاذ إجراءات فورية لتجنب هذا الاحتمال، وممارسة الضغط على روسيا لوقف هجماتها على البنية التحتية للطاقة. وأضاف أنه إذا لم تنجح هذه الجهود، فعلى الدول الأوروبية التنسيق والاستعداد لحالات الطوارئ لمواجهة العواقب المحتملة لأي حادث نووي. 38 دولة تدعم النداء والهيئات التي أطلقت هذا النداء هي رابطة رؤساء السلطات الأوروبية المختصة بالحماية من الإشعاع، ورابطة الهيئات التنظيمية النووية في أوروبا الغربية، ورابطة رؤساء سلطات السلامة الإشعاعية في دول الشمال. وتمثل هذه الهيئات مجتمعة 38 دولة، من بينها جميع دول الاتحاد الأوروبي والولايات المتحدة وبريطانيا وكندا واليابان. 3 محطات نووية توفر 80% من الطاقة تضم أوكرانيا أربع محطات للطاقة النووية، ثلاث منها قيد التشغيل، وتوفر نحو 80 في المئة من الطاقة المستخدمة خلال هذا الشتاء. أما المحطة الرابعة، زابوريجيا، وهي الأكبر في أوروبا، فتقع قرب خط المواجهة وتخضع لسيطرة روسيا. ولا تنتج المحطة حالياً الكهرباء، وتعتمد على مصدر طاقة خارجي للحفاظ على برودة المواد النووية وتجنب حدوث انصهار.

items.title: Armenian National Gallery opens first exhibition with AI-generated art
items.author: Arshaluys Barseghyan
items.preview: The exhibition is part of AI Days 2026 initiative.
items.content: The poster for Index of Pressure, the first exhibition featuring AI-generated art at the Armenian National Gallery. " /> The Armenian National Gallery opened its first exhibition featuring AI-generated art over the weekend. Titled Index of Pressure , the exhibition by interdisciplinary artist Sona Abgaryan combines AI-generated works with painting and sculpture. The exhibition is part of the nationwide AI Days 2026 initiative, organised by the UN Development Programme’s SDG Innovation Lab and Armenia’s Ministry of High-Tech Industry and AI. It comes as Armenia seeks to develop its AI industry, with Firebird officially opening the largest AI data centre of the region in August 2026. Firebird opens region’s largest AI data centre in Armenia The $5 billion Hrazdan facility is Armenia’s biggest step towards becoming a global AI hub, but still raises questions about its use of water and electricity. OC Media Ani Ghulinyan It features a multimedia installation bringing together ‘an AI-generated video, images printed on canvas, and a 3D-printed sculpture’. ‘The advent of generative artificial intelligence raises profound questions about the future of human experience. Will AI expand our understanding of reality and human agency, or lead us to the dystopias depicted in sci-films like the Blade Runner and the Matrix?’, the National Gallery’s description of the exhibition read. It went on to describe the exhibition as ‘drawing on Hollywood cinema, Baroque painting, advertising photography, and video games’, with the artist creating ‘a surreal universe of seductive yet disjointed imagery’. The exhibition addresses a key question: ‘will AI expand human creative capabilities and perceptions of reality, or will it create new limitations?’, the state-run media outlet Armenpress reported . ‘While working with AI, I constantly drew parallels with human relationships. They are very similar, because the limitations of AI remind me of the expectations we have in human relationships and how those expectations are not fulfilled. It is interesting to work within limitations and try to find new ways’, Abgaryan was quoted by Armenpress saying. The exhibition will remain open until 29 November.

items.title: Three men found guilty of Boris Nemtsov’s murder reportedly freed from prison, living in Chechnya
items.author: Elizaveta Chukharova
items.preview: Proekt’s reporting indicates that all five men convicted of the opposition politician’s murder are now free.
items.content: Three Chechen men convicted in the murder of Russian opposition politician Boris Nemtsov — Zaur Dadaev and brothers Anzor and Shadid Gubashev — have reportedly been released from prison early and are now living in Chechnya, according to an investigation by the independent Russian media outlet Proekt (‘Project’) , published on Monday. According to the journalists, the three Chechen men signed contracts with Russia’s Defence Ministry, which enabled them to leave prison. However, instead of being sent to fight in Ukraine, they returned to civilian life in Chechnya. A source cited by Proekt said they had been instructed to lead a ‘quiet life’ and avoid attracting attention, otherwise they could be sent back to prison. Boris Nemtsov, a former deputy prime minister of the Russian government and one of the country’s leading opposition figures, was shot dead on 27 February 2015 on the Bolshoi Moskvoretsky Bridge in Moscow, near the Kremlin. In July 2017, the Moscow District Military Court sentenced five men from Chechnya to prison terms ranging from 11 to 20 years. However, the person or people who ordered the murder have never been identified. Zaur Dadaev, whom the court identified as firing the fatal shot at Nemtsov, was sentenced to 20 years in prison. According to Proekt , he left a facility in Irkutsk Region on 24 October 2024 and is now living in the village of Yukarchoy, about 80 kilometres from Grozny. Anzor Gubashev was sentenced to 19 years in prison, while his brother Shadid received a 16-year sentence. According to the investigation, both have also returned to Chechnya, have wives and live in Grozny. Proekt have based their findings on prison records, which in some cases is circumstantial, such as that for Dadaev’s release. Journalists found that his employment record at Prison No 3 in Irkutsk contained an entry dated 24 October 2024 stating that he had been dismissed ‘in connection with his transfer’. Similar wording was used when prisoners left the facility to be sent to fight in the war. However, the journalists found no records of Dadaev arriving at another prison. The journalists also cite records showing that Dadaev registered as living in Yukarchoy and repaid a bank debt of ₽1.2 million ($14,500) in autumn 2026. Previously, bailiffs had made no attempts to recover the debt from him for nine years. According to Proekt , the Gubashev brothers were also released in 2024. After his conviction, Shadid Gubashev served his sentence at the Polar Wolf prison in the Yamalo-Nenets Region, the same facility where Aleksei Navalny was killed. In 2021, he was transferred to a prison in Chernokozovo, Chechnya. Anzor Gubashev also arrived at the Chernokozovo facility in December 2024. A source cited by Proekt claims that the brothers were released from this prison shortly. Proekt sent enquiries to Russian law enforcement agencies but received no response. Another man convicted in Nemtsov’s murder, Temirlan Eskerkhanov, was released from prison in 2024 after signing a contract with the Defence Ministry. The Russian independent media outlet Novaya Gazeta Europe reported that he serves in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Mariupol, guarding a steelworks factory. The fifth defendant in the case, Khamzat Bakhaev, completed his 11-year sentence this spring. Proekt 's latest reporting indicates that all five men convicted in connection with the politician’s murder are now free. Investigators named Ruslan Mukhudinov, a driver for Ruslan Geremeev, former deputy commander of the Chechen Sever battalion, as the organiser of the crime. Mukhudinov is on an international wanted list. Nemtsov’s relatives and investigative journalists have pointed to the possible involvement in organising the murder of people from Ramzan Kadyrov’s circle, including Adam Delimkhanov and members of the Geremeev family. In July 2023, the European Court of Human Rights ruled that the investigation into Nemtsov’s murder had been ineffective. The court said Russian investigators had failed to properly examine information concerning the possible involvement of senior Chechen officials and security personnel in organising the crime.

items.title: Musk backs campaign to reinstate ousted Nvidia boss
items.author: RT
items.preview: Elon Musk has joined other Silicon Valley executives in backing a petition calling for Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO Read Full Article at RT.com
items.content: Jensen Huang stepped down last week following reports of an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy Billionaire tech entrepreneur Elon Musk has joined a growing campaign by Silicon Valley heavyweights to bring back ousted Nvidia boss Jensen Huang. Huang stepped down following reports of an extramarital affair with a woman suspected by US officials of spying for China. More than 176,000 people have signed the online ‘Stand with Jensen’ petition calling for the reinstatement of Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and turned the Californian-based company into the world’s leading supplier of advanced chips used to power AI. Besides Musk, the campaign has attracted support from Tim Sweeney, founder and CEO of Epic Games, and Garry Tan, president of startup accelerator Y Combinator. Another signatory, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, who now heads robotics and AI company Atoms, described Huang as “one of the great builders of our time,” saying that “liberty and civilizational progress” depended on him. Read more Who wanted Nvidia’s Huang out? ‘Honeypot’ scandal raises questions over AI power struggle More than 8,800 signatories have identified themselves as Nvidia employees, representing nearly 21% of the chipmaker’s reported workforce of 42,000, according to the petition website. The petition’s organizers argue that Huang, who led Nvidia for 33 years, should be reinstated, at least “pending an independent investigation and clear evidence that his removal serves the company.” US officials have reportedly suspected the woman, Chinese business executive Alice Huang, who is not related to the Nvidia co-founder, of working for Beijing. However, the US Justice Department has acknowledged that no conclusion has been reached about the espionage allegations, which China has dismissed as unsubstantiated. Nvidia has launched an internal investigation into the allegations, while the FBI is also reportedly examining the claims. Huang, 63, has agreed to testify before congressional committees over the matter. Read more Ex-Nvidia boss faces Congress grilling over ‘Chinese honeypot’ scandal According to the Financial Times, Huang is interested in returning to his former position. A source close to him told the newspaper that a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives is being assembled to lobby for his reinstatement, with plans to seek support from the White House. However, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on Sunday that Nvidia should look for a new CEO from “outside” the company. “They need a dramatic shake-up,” he said. Bessent also urged Nvidia to explain whether it knowingly allowed its most advanced chips to reach China, arguing that investigating the matter was more important than examining Huang’s personal affairs. The scandal has fueled calls from both Republican and Democratic lawmakers to tighten restrictions on advanced US chip exports to China. Senators Elizabeth Warren and Jim Banks have urged Congress to pass legislation allowing it to block certain sales, while other lawmakers have demanded an immediate halt to exports. Beijing has warned against using the unproven espionage allegations as a pretext for imposing further technological restrictions.

items.title: At ECO moot, Dar calls for translating 'collective commitments into concrete action'
items.author: none@none.com (News Desk, Ameer Hamza)
items.preview: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar closed out the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers (COM) in Islamabad on Monday with a call for countries to translate their commitments into action. Pakistan, which holds the ECO ch
items.content: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar closed out the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers (COM) in Islamabad on Monday with a call for countries to translate their commitments into action. Pakistan, which holds the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27, hosted the meeting under the theme “Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO”. The deputy premier, who chaired the meeting, expressed his “sincere appreciation to all delegations” for their constructive engagement during the meeting. “The deliberations today have reaffirmed our shared commitment to regional economic cooperation and integration,” Dar said. He termed the adoption of the Strategic Goals of Economic Cooperation 2035 an “important milestone in charting the future course of our organisation over the next decade”, saying that it provided a shared framework to advance regional priorities alongside the Islamabad Communiqué. “Our task now is to translate our collective commitments into concrete action,” he added. “This will require clear priorities, realistic timelines, and effective follow-up mechanisms.” He highlighted regional cooperation as a central pillar of Pakistan’s foreign policy and noted that the country had consistently advocated a “stronger, more effective and responsive” ECO that harnessed “geographical proximity, historical bonds and economic complementarities”. Dar underscored Pakistan’s commitment to advancing the ECO agenda as the chair of the organisation and to working with all institutions and member states to strengthen regional connectivity, facilitate intra-regional trade and promote mutually beneficial economic cooperation. He looked forward to welcoming the countries back for the 31st COM meeting in 2027, saying, “Let us build on the momentum generated here so that our next meeting can take stock of tangible progress in advancing our shared priorities.” In addition, he wished Iran success in hosting the upcoming 18th ECO summit on Dec 3-4. The deputy premier thanked all member states, as well as the secretary general and his team, ECO permanent representatives, and senior officials for their support. Later in the day, Dar held a media briefing on the meeting alongside ECO Secretary General Asad Majeed Khan and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar. Araghchi calls for sustainable energy mechanism At the ECO meeting, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stressed the need for a reliable and sustainable regional energy mechanism during his address. The Iranian FM spoke about the US-Israeli war on Iran , which has also resulted in the choking of key fuel supply routes — the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab . “Our region needs not only an independent security framework but also a reliable and sustainable regional energy mechanism to safeguard energy flows, ensure stable supplies, reduce external vulnerabilities and enhance collective resilience against geopolitical shocks and disruptions,” Araghchi said, according to a transcript of his speech provided by the Iranian embassy in Pakistan. Araghchi said ECO was moving “beyond its traditional role towards becoming an effective platform for collective action, strengthened cooperation and joint efforts”. He said the shift would enable member states “to address emerging challenges and contribute to an inclusive and equitable global economic order”. He stressed the need for a “modern, new-generation, more inclusive, effective and operational trade agreement” that would benefit the region. Referring to the US war on Iran, Araghchi said, “Iran has remained committed to diplomatic engagement and peaceful solutions.” He added, however, that the US had opted for a different course of action, which was “marked by aggression, threats, targeted assassinations, economic coercion, and blockades, in flagrant violation of international law and the UN Charter”. He underscored that Iran had “no inherent dispute” with countries in the region, adding that “the territories, airspace and facilities of the regional countries must not be used as platforms for launching attacks against each other”. “Iran’s legitimate defensive measures are directed exclusively at the targets and military bases of the aggressors and should in no way be construed as actions against the peoples or governments of the neighbouring countries,” Araghchi said. He also called attention to Palestine , describing the genocide in Gaza as “the most pressing international crisis”. Condemning the destruction and killings at the hands of Israeli forces in Palestine, he said, “We are witnessing the intensification of expansionist policies by the Israeli regime in the West Bank and occupied Al-Quds.” “This is a moment that calls for concrete action, collective responsibility, and an end to silence and indifference.” He concluded his speech by reiterating that Iran’s stability and prosperity were “intrinsically linked” to those of other ECO members. Pakistan calls on Afghanistan to address terror concerns Araghchi’s remarks followed the opening speech by DPM Dar. In those remarks, Dar said Pakistan desired a peaceful, prosperous and stable Afghanistan , but meaningful progress towards regional cooperation required the Afghan authorities to address the legitimate security concerns of neighbouring countries, particularly the threat of terrorism. He added that a stable Afghanistan, at peace with itself and all its neighbours and fully integrated into the ECO framework, would benefit the Afghan people as well as the wider region by opening up avenues for trade, transit and economic cooperation. “At the same time, meaningful progress requires the Afghan authorities to address the legitimate security concerns of the neighbouring countries, particularly the threat of terrorism,” Dar said. He stressed that a secure and stable environment was essential for sustained regional economic partnerships, adding that these considerations remained central to Pakistan’s broader connectivity agenda. “Regional connectivity rests on more than the routes that link us. It depends upon trust between states and confidence that international commitments will be honoured. Unresolved disputes and the non-fulfilment of international obligations can erode that trust and impede economic progress,” said Dar. The foreign minister emphasised that respect for international law and treaties is essential to enduring economic partnerships between countries. Outlining Pakistan’s priorities during its chairmanship of the ECO, Dar identified five key areas of focus, including expanding trade and investment, strengthening regional connectivity, advancing the ECO Trade Agreement, building regional resilience and promoting human development. The foreign minister said the region’s natural resources, energy reserves, agricultural potential and strategic location offered considerable opportunities for economic cooperation, but realising that potential required functioning transport corridors, efficient border procedures and predictable transit arrangements. He said Pakistan would work towards wider market access, stronger regional value chains and greater private sector participation, particularly by small and medium-sized enterprises, to boost trade and investment among member states. “Closer interaction among our business communities can help translate commercial potential into greater trade and investment.” Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in a cordial exchange with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, Tajikistan Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Muhriddin, OIC Secretary General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed and ECO Secretary General Dr. Asad Majeed Khan on the sidelines of the 30th ECO Council of Ministers Meeting in Islamabad on Nov 16. — ForeignOfficePk/X On connectivity, Dar said Pakistan would seek to improve transport and transit links between Central Asia, South Asia and Pakistani ports on the Arabian Sea. Harmonised customs procedures, efficient border management and predictable transit arrangements were essential to making regional trade routes commercially viable, he added. The foreign minister also highlighted the need to advance the ECO Trade Agreement, saying the negotiating strategy and roadmap approved by ECO trade ministers in November 2025 provided a basis for modernising the agreement. Pakistan would support efforts to develop a more effective, inclusive and digitally enabled regional trade framework, he said. On regional resilience, Dar called for closer cooperation in disaster preparedness, early warning systems, sustainable water management and climate-resilient infrastructure, noting that climate change and growing pressure on water and energy resources posed serious challenges to regional economies. He also underscored the importance of human development, particularly in education, research, innovation and vocational training, saying greater opportunities in these areas could equip young people with skills needed by changing economies. Promoting entrepreneurship and professional exchanges would further strengthen regional integration, he added. The foreign minister maintained that the five priorities were interconnected and their success would depend on collective efforts by member states. He expressed Pakistan’s readiness to work with ECO members and the organisation’s secretariat on initiatives relating to trade facilitation, transit connectivity and disaster preparedness. Regional peace and diplomatic efforts Dar cautioned that peace and stability were essential for economic development, warning that conflict and insecurity in the region could disrupt trade routes, energy supplies, investment and economic projects. “Peace and development reinforce each other,” he said. He added that Pakistan remained “deeply concerned about conflict and instability” in the region. “Their consequences extend beyond national boundaries, disrupting trade routes, energy supplies, investment, and the economic projects of our peoples.” He said that Pakistan has consistently advocated for “the peaceful resolution of disputes through dialogue and diplomacy in accordance with international law and the United Nations Charter”. Referring to Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts in the US-Israeli war on Iran, Dar said, “Pakistan will continue these diplomatic efforts in support of dialogue, de-escalation, and lasting regional stability.” He said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir “remained closely engaged with brotherly countries and international partners to facilitate peaceful outcomes”. ECO delegation heads call on PM Shehbaz Separately, the foreign ministers and delegation heads of ECO member states paid a joint call on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, according to a handout issued by the PM’s Office. The premier thanked them for their participation in the meeting and reaffirmed Pakistan’s “strong commitment” to ECO objectives. He reiterated his government’s resolve to promote regional cooperation, connectivity and economic integration within the ECO member states. The premier appreciated the meeting’s successful conclusion and welcomed the adoption of the Islamabad Communique and the Strategic Goals of Economic Cooperation 2035, describing them as “important steps” towards strengthening the organisation and advancing shared regional priorities. The premier highlighted Pakistan’s ECO chairmanship and emphasised the need to translate the organisation’s collective vision into concrete, result-oriented initiatives that deliver “tangible benefits” to the region’s people. Furthermore, the handout said that the premier called for enhanced cooperation in trade and investment, transport and transit connectivity, energy, information and communication technology, and sustainable development. “He stressed the importance of effective implementation of existing ECO agreements and strengthening institutional mechanisms to accelerate regional economic integration,” the statement said. PM Shehbaz highlighted the country’s strategic geographical location. He reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to enhancing regional connectivity through road, rail and multimodal transport corridors, including linkages with the ports of Karachi, Port Qasim and Gwadar, to facilitate access to regional and international markets, particularly for landlocked ECO member states. “Underlining Pakistan’s commitment to dialogue and diplomacy for the peaceful resolution of disputes, the premier stressed the importance of collective efforts to address threats to regional security,” the statement added. He also expressed Pakistan’s resolve to work closely with all member states and the ECO secretariat to further strengthen the organisation during its chairmanship. “The prime minister reaffirmed that Pakistan looked forward to welcoming ECO member states again in 2027 for the next Council of Ministers Meeting and the ECO summit,” the handout concluded. Senior officials meet to finalise agenda Senior officials of the ECO finalised the agenda and draft Islamabad Communiqué on Sunday, ahead of the organisation’s COM meeting. According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA), the Senior Officials Meeting (SOM) was held on Nov 15 under the chairmanship of Foreign Secretary Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad. The meeting was attended by senior officials from ECO member states, representatives of the ECO Secretariat, and delegates from the organisation’s specialised agencies and regional institutions. The officials reviewed preparations for the ministerial meeting and finalised its agenda and the draft Islamabad Communiqué for consideration by the foreign ministers. They also reviewed the activities undertaken by the ECO Secretariat during the year, including ongoing programmes and initiatives, outcomes of sectoral ministerial meetings, and the work of subsidiary bodies and specialised institutions, the ministry said. Administrative and financial matters of the organisation also came under discussion, with participants exchanging views on measures to improve its effectiveness. The SOM serves as a preparatory forum for the ECO COM, enabling member states to assess progress, discuss issues of mutual interest and build consensus on proposals and draft documents ahead of ministerial-level deliberations.

items.title: Senior Kiev cops likely protecting call center mafia from EU scrutiny – Western investigators
items.author: RT
items.preview: Western officials have reported evidence that corruption in Ukrainian law enforcement is hampering investigations into scam-call centers Read Full Article at RT.com
items.content: Officials in Estonia and Austria have claimed they have been blocked from investigating Ukraine’s massive scam sector known to target countries in the bloc Sensitive information about foreign criminal investigations targeting Ukrainian organized crime has been leaked through government channels in Kiev to the suspects, according to media reports citing European law enforcement officials. Allegations that senior Ukrainian officials were working hand-in-glove with crime bosses to profit from fraudulent call centers, drug trafficking and other criminal enterprises triggered a new corruption scandal in Kiev earlier this month. Recent statements by officials in Estonia and Austria lend weight to claims that elements of Vladimir Zelensky’s government have been shielding criminals from Western law enforcement. A general in the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) and senior National Police officials have been accused of accepting protection money from a criminal syndicate allegedly led by Mexico-based mastermind Egor Burkin. The scandal was largely overlooked in the Western press, though it is thought to generate up to $1 billion every month, while RT has covered it in detail. An interview published on Monday by Ukrainskaya Pravda details Estonia’s experience attempting to shut down scam-call centers targeting citizens in the Baltic EU state from Ukraine and the discouraging results of requests for cooperation sent to Kiev. Read more ‘Carthage must be destroyed’: How Ukrainian cops and criminals worked hand-in-hand “When we asked to hit call centers, fraudsters would manage to flee before local police arrived. This happened quite often,” Jaagup Toompuu, head of Estonia’s national anti-fraud police unit, told the Ukrainian outlet. Asked about the latest corruption scandal in Kiev, he said that if the allegations were confirmed, the “probability is high that tips not only from Estonia but also other nations regarding the scam centers ended up in the hands of criminals.” Toompuu also acknowledged some positive experiences with Ukrainian law enforcement, including cooperation that resulted in the successful prosecution of Artur Ermolaev in Estonia. The son of Ukraine-born businessman Vadim Ermolaev received a suspended sentence in the Baltic state in April after agreeing to pay a multi-million-euro fine to compensate victims of fraudulent call centers he was accused of operating. His father was targeted in a Ukrainian-organized bombing attack in Monaco earlier this year. Toompuu was reluctant to criticize Ukrainian law enforcement because of the country’s war with Russia but stressed that the cybercrime threat was serious and ultimately had to be addressed by Ukrainian authorities themselves, since “I cannot order our special forces guys to storm Ukrainian homes.” Read more Ukraine’s scam call centers paid $370 mn a year in bribes – alleged cartel boss The problem of corruption within Ukrainian law enforcement is also an open secret in Austria, Der Standard reported on Saturday. Evidence released this month by the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU) included an image from a police event that the agency said had been leaked to Burkin by another senior suspect, alleged crime boss Andrey Osipov. The slide contained details of an investigation targeting Burkin. The photograph was taken at an Interpol event hosted by a European country, the Austrian newspaper reported, adding that the leak was known to the country’s Federal Criminal Police. Burkin had spent several weeks in Austria before sharing the image in April 2025. He was investigated in the country over his use of a heavily modified vehicle equipped with a smoke bomb intended as an anti-theft device, according to the report. Coincidentally, Vienna has become the place of residence of former Ukrainian Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko, who fled Ukraine in September after the first allegations in NABU’s “Operation Carthage” became public. Read more Who is the Ukrainian oligarch allegedly targeted in the Monaco bombing? Those accusations targeted Sergey Kropiva, who headed cybercrime prosecutions under Kravchenko and was accused of operating a protection racket for scam-call centers on behalf of his boss. Kravchenko himself has not been formally accused of any crime. Ukrainian media have previously identified several other former senior officials who left office in recent years and moved to Vienna, including former National Bank governor Kirill Shevchenko, former Constitutional Court chairman Alexander Tupitsky and former MP Andrey Kholodov. A separate major criminal case involving Ukrainian nationals made headlines almost a year ago, when the 21-year-old son of a former deputy mayor of Kharkov was found murdered in a burned-out car in the Austrian capital. Two Ukrainian nationals, the stepson of a former Ukrainian ambassador to Bulgaria and a former customs official, were identified as suspects in the killing, which investigators believe was motivated by financial extortion. In early October, Austrian police detained two people suspected of being operatives of Ukraine’s military intelligence agency HUR who had allegedly been conducting surveillance on Kravchenko. The bombing attack in Monaco was allegedly masterminded by an active HUR operative and an unofficial SBU asset. The two suspects were arrested in Ukraine over the alleged killing of the attack’s main perpetrator, a Ukrainian woman.

items.title: Lukaku retires from international football
items.author: Jamaica Observer
items.content: Belgium's all-time leading men's goalscorer Romelu Lukaku has retired from international football after 16 years representing his country. The 33-year-old Fenerbahce striker made the announcement in an Instagram post, saying he had “enjoyed every single moment” of playing for Belgium. According to BBC Sport, Lukaku made his international debut in 2010 and scored 94 goals in 135 appearances, making him the fifth highest men's international goalscorer of all time, behind Sunil Chhetri, Ali Daei, Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. He scored eight goals across four World Cups and six goals at three European Championships. In his farewell message, Lukaku thanked his team-mates and coaches for their support throughout his international career. “These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team... I went through every emotion possible,” he wrote. He also thanked Belgian supporters and expressed pride in representing his country at four World Cups and three European Championships. “I’m at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing. It was enjoyable. I’m grateful,” he added. Lukaku missed Belgium's recent Nations League victory over Turkey because of a hip injury and was an unused substitute in Sunday's 4-1 win over Italy, which secured the team's place in the competition's last eight, BBC said. In 2023, he scored 14 goals in eight appearances during the Euro 2024 qualifying campaign, setting a record for the most goals by a player in a single European Championship qualifying campaign, it added. Belgium team-mate Kevin De Bruyne also paid tribute to Lukaku, posting a photograph of the pair on Instagram and describing his contribution to the team and country as immeasurable.

items.title: Mauritania orders EU fishing vessels to leave its waters
items.author: RT
items.preview: Mauritania has ordered EU fishing vessels to stop operations and leave its waters after a five-year fishing protocol expired Read Full Article at RT.com
items.content: Ships from the bloc have been told to leave after a five-year protocol expired Mauritania has ordered EU fishing vessels to halt operations and leave its waters following the expiry of a five-year fisheries protocol. The country’s coast guard warned that vessels continuing to fish after the November 14 deadline could face legal penalties, according to local news agency Madar. “As a result, all ships operating in the Mauritanian fishing zone are required to stop their fishing activities and join the port of Nouadhibou today," the coast guard’s circular said. The order followed the expiry of the fisheries protocol, which had been in force since November 15, 2021. No replacement had been officially announced by either side before the deadline. Mauritania and the EU had maintained a fisheries partnership since 1987. Read more Russian scientists complete major study of African waters The protocol allowed vessels from ten EU countries, including Spain, France, Portugal, and the Netherlands, to catch up to 280,050 tonnes of fish annually in Mauritanian waters. In return, the EU provided €60.8 million ($70 million) per year, including an average of €3.3 million annually to support Mauritania’s fisheries sector, according to the European Commission. Negotiations on a new protocol had been underway since January, with four rounds of talks held without an agreement. In October, fisheries ministers from Spain, Portugal, the Netherlands, and Latvia urged EU Fisheries Commissioner Costas Kadis to accelerate negotiations and consider extending the existing arrangement if a new deal could not be reached. The four countries warned that a break in fishing access could have negative economic and social consequences for the sector. The European Commission submitted a revised proposal to Mauritania, while Kadis held further discussions with Mauritanian Fisheries Minister Aissata Lam in November. READ MORE: Dozens of migrants dead or missing off African coast – UN The expiry could affect 60 European vessels, including 25 based in Spain’s Andalusia region, and threaten around 500 direct and indirect jobs, Agence Europe reported, citing the Andalusian regional government. The Spanish authorities have also explored alternative fishing grounds, including waters off Guinea-Bissau, according to Madar.

items.title: Turkey launches regular cargo flights to Armenia as relations improve
items.author: Arshaluys Barseghyan
items.preview: The land border between Turkey and Armenia has been closed since 1993.
items.content: Turkish Cargo, the cargo transportation service of the flag carrier Turkish Airlines, completed its first scheduled cargo flight between Istanbul and Yerevan on Sunday, Turkish sources report. No further details have been provided about the volume or nature of the cargo transported. In 1993, Turkey unilaterally severed diplomatic relations with Armenia and closed its shared land border in solidarity with Azerbaijan during the First Nagorno-Karabakh War. The border has remained closed since then, including for cargo transit by rail. ‘Executed through the coordination of regional management and the operations team, this special flight provides efficient and reliable transport solutions between the two countries while continuing to expand the global logistics network’, Turkey-based aviation website Aeroportist reported . The cargo operation follows the launch of regular passenger flights by Turkish Airlines on the Istanbul–Yerevan–Istanbul route in March 2026, as the two countries have taken steps towards normalising relations. Previously, the only air connection between Yerevan and Istanbul was provided by the Turkish low-cost carrier Pegasus, after Armenian airline FlyOne Armenia was forced to suspend its operations through Turkish airspace due to a Turkish government-imposed ban in 2023. Turkish Airlines to launch Yerevan flights amid apparent thaw in Armenia–Turkey relations The airline has not yet provided a start date or potential flight frequency. OC Media OC Media The latest cargo operation comes days after Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan met Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Antalya on the sidelines of the COP31 Leaders’ Summit. The two leaders ‘discussed the process’ of normalising bilateral relations and ‘emphasised the importance of advancing this process toward a logical conclusion’. Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan (left) and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan (right) meet on the sidelines of the Leaders’ Summit held in Antalya, Turkey within the framework of COP31. Official photo. Following the meeting, Pashinyan expressed confidence that ‘in the near future we will achieve full normalisation of relations with Turkey’, adding that during their meeting, ‘we both noted that we have made progress and are very close to the final step: establishing diplomatic relations and fully opening the borders’. Despite a 2022 agreement to allow third-country citizens and diplomats to cross their shared land border, Turkey has linked its full reopening to progress in the Armenia–Azerbaijan peace process. In turn, Armenian officials have accused Azerbaijan of obstructing the normalisation process in April. Yerevan says Azerbaijan hindering normalisation with Turkey The Armenia–Turkey land border remains closed despite an agreement to allow crossings for third-party nationals. OC Media Arshaluys Barseghyan The cargo flight, however, is the latest in a series of developments in bilateral relations this year. In October, Armenia and Turkey discussed restoring and commissioning the Gyumri–Kars transmission line as Yerevan pushes to secure alternative energy sources and to normalise ties with Ankara. Earlier, in May, Pashinyan announced that the Akhalkalaki–Kars railway connecting Georgia and Turkey ‘is now open’ for Armenian exports and imports. That same month, Turkey lifted restrictions on trade with Armenia, allowing bilateral trade to proceed without goods having to be re-registered in a third country before crossing the border. Separately, Armenian and Turkish business representatives held several meetings. As of 1 January, Armenia and Turkey ‘simplified’ visa procedures for holders of diplomatic, special, and service passports.

items.title: India signs AI supply chain pact
items.author: RT
items.preview: India and the US are among nine signatories to the San Francisco declaration on artificial intelligence supply chains ahead of a Quad meet Read Full Article at RT.com
items.content: Ten nations have pledged cooperation on sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure ahead of a Quad gathering in Manila India has signed a US-led declaration to bolster artificial intelligence supply chain security ahead of a meeting of the Quad in Manila aimed at countering China’s control over critical minerals. The San Francisco Declaration is a corollary to the Pax Silica agreement – a US-backed initiative to bolster AI supply chains – as Western nations worry about advances in AI by Chinese companies and their growing clout. The accord is aimed at facilitating a “common understanding of the sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure that underpin Super Intelligence supply chains.” Super Intelligence is US President Donald Trump’s favorite term for AI. The declaration, under the Pax Silica framework, also aims to establish a common list of sensitive technologies and supply chains supporting AI development that need greater protection. In February, India formally joined the Pax Silica initiative to boost collaboration on semiconductors, critical minerals, energy, advanced manufacturing and AI infrastructure. New Delhi said then that the alliance would deepen engagement on critical technologies and supply chain resilience under the India-US Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership. Read more India joins US-led Pax Silica alliance Pax Silica gives New Delhi an opportunity to tap billions of dollars in AI and technology investment and cement its role as an alternative to China. India has launched a string of initiatives including the National Critical Minerals Mission, and announced rare earth corridors for the mining, processing, research, and manufacturing of Rare Earth Permanent Magnets (REPMs). New Delhi imports 85%-90% of its rare earth requirements from China. These elements are primary ingredients in making the magnets used as key components in everything from smartphones to electric vehicle motors and missile guidance systems. Beijing now accounts for more than 60% of global rare earth processing capacity. The San Francisco Declaration comes ahead of Trump’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Shenzhen Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum on Thursday, and also follows the alleged Chinese espionage scandal which brought down Nvidia founder Jensen Huang. The US has, meanwhile, accused China of not fulfilling the terms of the trade truce between the two nations reached late last year. Washington has urged China to increase exports of rare earths ahead of the Trump-Xi meeting. The US, Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, and the UK signed the San Francisco declaration. Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands, and the European Commission are expected to sign later, US Under-Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg was quoted as saying by the Financial Times.

items.title: Army Commander or Lebanon’s Self-Appointed Guardian?
items.author: Makram Rabah
items.preview: A handout photo provided by the Lebanese […] The post Army Commander or Lebanon’s Self-Appointed Guardian? appeared first on Nowlebanon .
items.content: A handout photo provided by the Lebanese presidency on March 13, 2025 shows Lebanese President Joseph Aoun (R) congratulating the newly appointed Army Commander in Chief Rodolphe Haykal, at the presidential palace of Baabda, east of Beirut. (Photo by Lebanese Presidency / AFP) / General Rodolph Haykal speaks to the Lebanese in the language of the 1990s, when Syrian tutelage turned questioning authority into grounds for suspicion and reduced patriotism to obedience. At a recent meeting at army headquarters in Yarzeh, he declared that those who criticize the military without understanding its work and seek to tarnish its image are acting in a manner “incompatible with national loyalty.” In doing so, he put criticism on trial and appointed himself the arbiter of who belongs to Lebanon. The army commander is a public servant, paid from a treasury funded by Lebanese citizens, including those who criticize him. It is disgraceful for a public servant to treat citizens as troops under his command. His rank gives him no authority over their opinions, and their objections are not acts of insubordination. He is entitled to answer criticism with facts. He is also obliged to account for his performance. No citizen needs to graduate from staff college to ask why Hezbollah’s arsenal remains beyond the authority of the state. Even soldiers do not surrender their rights or dignity by putting on a uniform. They are entitled to seek redress through lawful channels when the leadership fails them or undermines their standing as defenders of the country. Civilians, meanwhile, are not subject to military discipline in the first place. Lebanon’s constitutional preamble places freedom of opinion at the heart of the republic, and Article 13 guarantees freedom of expression within the limits of the law. The commander is bound by those guarantees, whatever his rank. This is the Aounist mentality that Michel Aoun entrenched in his approach to the state and the army, reducing the institution to the person of its commander. Within this logic, questioning the commander becomes an insult to the army, and disagreeing with him an attack on the nation. This is the Aounist mentality that Michel Aoun entrenched in his approach to the state and the army, reducing the institution to the person of its commander. Within this logic, questioning the commander becomes an insult to the army, and disagreeing with him an attack on the nation. Haykal revives that legacy when he casts doubt on his critics’ patriotism and effectively demands that they prove it through silence. His recital of achievements recalls a student who has not finished his homework but keeps insisting that he has, then resents the teacher who asks to see it. Repetition does not earn a passing grade. Rehabilitating Qlayaat airport is worthwhile, but it does not resolve the question of Hezbollah’s weapons. Soldiers’ sacrifices deserve a leadership that is honest about its performance. Those sacrifices must never become a shield behind which senior officers evade accountability. In January 2026, the army command announced that it had achieved the objectives of the first phase of its disarmament plan south of the Litani River. It described operational control over the areas under its authority, excluding positions still under Israeli occupation, while acknowledging that work on tunnels and unexploded ordnance continued. Haykal presented his report to the cabinet, which asked the army to prepare for the next phase. In January 2026, the army command announced that it had achieved the objectives of the first phase of its disarmament plan south of the Litani River. It described operational control over the areas under its authority, excluding positions still under Israeli occupation, while acknowledging that work on tunnels and unexploded ordnance continued. Haykal presented his report to the cabinet, which asked the army to prepare for the next phase. Hezbollah then returned to war. Reuters subsequently reported on its battles in Bint Jbeil and its efforts to rebuild its military capabilities with Iranian funding. The army’s assurances did not survive the test of events. The Lebanese are entitled to ask: Were the weapons never removed, or did they return? What does operational control mean if Hezbollah can once again seize the military initiative? Nor did Israel’s renewed occupation materialize out of thin air. Hassan Nasrallah chose to open his “support front” on October 8, 2023. Hezbollah attacked Israeli positions, setting off an exchange that eventually escalated into full-scale war and invasion. Hezbollah returned to battle in March 2026 in support of Iran. Condemning the occupation does not absolve those who dragged Lebanon into these wars and denied its people the right to stay out of them. Israel now explicitly makes its withdrawal conditional on Hezbollah’s disarmament. Waiting for that withdrawal while preserving the arsenal, even if it is rebranded as merely symbolic, is selling the Lebanese an illusion. Israel now explicitly makes its withdrawal conditional on Hezbollah’s disarmament. Waiting for that withdrawal while preserving the arsenal, even if it is rebranded as merely symbolic, is selling the Lebanese an illusion. The weapons supply Israel with a continuing pretext for remaining in southern Lebanon. Blaming Israel alone for Lebanon’s lack of sovereignty while protecting the party that usurps it from within is a political farce that absolves Hezbollah of the consequences of its choices. Even Haykal’s description of the UN Interim Force in Lebanon, UNIFIL, as a “living record” of the conflict exposes the limits of his vision of the state. Lebanon needs institutions capable of preventing the next catastrophe. Keeping witnesses to the last one is no substitute for exercising sovereignty. Yet reducing this problem to Haykal alone grants President Joseph Aoun an acquittal he has not earned. Aoun is commander-in-chief of the armed forces, which Article 49 of the constitution places under the authority of the Council of Ministers Yet reducing this problem to Haykal alone grants President Joseph Aoun an acquittal he has not earned. Aoun is commander-in-chief of the armed forces, which Article 49 of the constitution places under the authority of the Council of Ministers. Political responsibility begins at the presidential palace in Baabda and extends to the cabinet. When an army commander starts defining the limits of permissible national debate, the president must enforce the limits of the commander’s authority and take responsibility for the policies he implements. Aoun has repeatedly framed the handling of Hezbollah’s weapons around the need to avoid civil war. Protecting Lebanese lives is a duty. Turning fear of confrontation into an open-ended excuse for delay, however, gives an armed organization a veto over the state. What is required is a plan carried out responsibly, with measurable stages and identifiable officials who can be held to account. To proclaim the state’s monopoly on force while treating its enforcement as a threat to stability is to turn the constitution into a promise that can be honored only with Hezbollah’s permission. The cabinet has already banned Hezbollah’s military and security activities and ordered the party to surrender its weapons. Why, then, are citizens expected to applaud while implementation remains an open question? The military leadership’s job is to carry out the decisions of the constitutional authorities and provide a clear account of what it has done. An officer swears to fulfill his duty and defend Lebanon. That oath requires him to protect the state, its constitutional order and the rights of its citizens against threats from abroad and from within. Hezbollah, by tying its weapons, funding and wars to Iran, performs an Iranian military role on Lebanese soil. Its members’ Lebanese citizenship does not confer national legitimacy on that regional project or oblige the army to accommodate it at the state’s expense. Aoun and the cabinet must hold the military leadership accountable. Haykal must answer the questions. Our right to speak takes precedence over any claim to guardianship. We will not accept a shabby Orwellian version of Lebanon where obedience is called patriotism and asking a question becomes treason Aoun and the cabinet must hold the military leadership accountable. Haykal must answer the questions. Our right to speak takes precedence over any claim to guardianship. We will not accept a shabby Orwellian version of Lebanon where obedience is called patriotism and asking a question becomes treason. The Lebanese are not waiting for certificates of belonging from Yarzeh. They expect a state that protects them from occupation and the rule of militias, and they will hold accountable everyone paid to serve them. This article was originally published in Elaph. Makram Rabah is the managing editor at Now Lebanon and an Assistant Professor at the American University of Beirut, Department of History. His book Conflict on Mount Lebanon: The Druze, the Maronites and Collective Memory (Edinburgh University Press) covers collective identities and the Lebanese Civil War. items.title: UN chief urges countries to rein in 'merciless' killer robots
items.author: none@none.com (AFP)
items.preview: The United Nations chief on Monday called on countries to work towards imposing strict and binding rules on the use of “merciless” lethal autonomous weapons systems, often dubbed “killer robots”. Warfare is undergoing a radical transformation as armies seek to capitalise on artif
items.content: The United Nations chief on Monday called on countries to work towards imposing strict and binding rules on the use of “merciless” lethal autonomous weapons systems, often dubbed “killer robots”. Warfare is undergoing a radical transformation as armies seek to capitalise on artificial intelligence to boost their fighting abilities by identifying and striking targets more quickly and accurately. Amid a chorus of warnings against handing the power of life and death to autonomous machines, country representatives have gathered for a conference at the UN in Geneva this week to debate whether to launch talks on binding rules for such weapons. “Take action to prevent the use and spread of these merciless weapons,” UN chief Antonio Guterres urged the conference in a video message. “I call on you to move towards negotiating a legally binding instrument to regulate autonomous weapon systems — including clear prohibitions and restrictions,” he said. “We must never stop shielding civilians from the carnage and devastation of armed conflict, and preventing unnecessary suffering.” Others have also warned of the dangers if lethal autonomous weapons systems, or LAWS, are permitted to select and kill targets without human intervention. Human Rights Watch said the meeting of the UN’s Review Conference of the Convention on Conventional Weapons (CCW) would leave civilians “dangerously exposed” if it failed to act decisively. High stakes The meeting brings together 128 countries to decide whether to open negotiations on legally binding rules. The discussions in Geneva are meanwhile expected to be challenging, with countries at odds and full consensus needed for any decisions. While many states are in favour of tighter rules, countries that have the technology are reluctant to have their hands tied. Even before Monday’s discussions could begin, Russia’s representative objected to observers — including the European Union and civil society — being permitted to participate in the debate. Campaigners suggested the Russian move, which forced the temporary suspension of the proceedings, was a bid to dodge criticism of its own alleged use of such weapons in Ukraine. “States must ensure that Russia, or any of the handful of governments blocking progress, are not allowed to hold the future hostage,” insisted Anna Hehir, head of military AI governance at the Future of Life Institute. “The stakes are too high.” The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) is calling for a ban on two categories of autonomous weapons: so-called “unpredictable autonomous weapons” and those designed or used to directly target humans. “States have a crucial responsibility to ensure that the future of warfare is not handed over to machines,” ICRC president Mirjana Spoljaric said ahead of the conference. “Future generations will judge whether leaders acted to prevent a world where machines autonomously kill humans.” ‘Carefully cultivated ambiguity’ But positions appear to be far apart. At the UN General Assembly last month, 163 states adopted a resolution calling for negotiations on rules governing autonomous weapons. Five countries voted against: the United States, Russia, Belarus, Israel and North Korea, which last week boasted of a new AI-enabled torpedo system. Nine abstained, including Iran, Saudi Arabia and China, which has maintained a “carefully cultivated ambiguity”, said Laure de Roucy-Rochegonde of the French Institute of International Relations. And while Washington has proposed a five-year process to develop a non-binding instrument, NGOs and the ICRC are advocating for a one-year timeline towards binding rules.
